simple.meaning: to be extinguished ; figuratively, to expire or be dried up
simple.inThisVerse: The selected word is tied to דָּעַךְ (H1846) in the Hebrew source text. Part of speech: v.
simple.whyItMatters: This word appears 9 times in the Hebrew Bible, so BibleIQ can compare how Scripture uses it across multiple passages.
simple.summary: דָּעַךְ (dâʻak) means to be extinguished ; figuratively, to expire or be dried up First listed occurrence: Isa 43 17.

definitions.short: to be extinguished ; figuratively, to expire or be dried up
definitions.usage: be extinct, consumed, put out, quenched.
definitions.full: H1846. daak [ דָּעַךְ ] verb go out, be extinguished (in poetry & especially Wisdom literature) (Aramaic דְּעִיךְ , ) — Qal Perfect 3masculine plural דָּֽעֲכוּ Isa 43:17 ; Imperfect יִדְעַךְ Prov 20:20 , יִדְעָ֑ךְ Job 18:5 4 t.; — go out, be extinguished , of lamp, always figurative, lamp of wicked (i.e. prosperity) רְשָׁעִים אוֺר 18:5 , ר ׳נֵר 18:6 ; 21:17 ; Prov 13:9 ; 20:20 ; 24:20 ; of hostile armies Isa 43:17 (|| כָּב֫וּ ). Niph`al Perfect 3plural נִדְעֲכוּ be made extinct, dried up , Job 6:17 (of brooks). Pu`al Perfect 3plural דֹּעֲכוּ of assailants, be extinguished, quenched , קוֺצִים כְּאֵשׁ Psa 118:12 ; but read perhaps בערו with ᵐ5 Bae & Che, see Che critical note . דַּעַת see below ידע . דפה (√ of following, meaning unknown; Late Hebrew דּוֺפִי is blemish, fault ).
